top3.headline: Data centers lost at the ballot box in the US midterms
top3.whyItMatters: If US opposition to building lasts, AI compute plans face delays and higher costs.

top3.headline: Claude Code lets failed safety hooks block agent actions
top3.whyItMatters: Agent guardrails can now fail closed, so a broken check stops the action instead of allowing it.

top3.headline: Grading errors silently reorder popular AI agent leaderboards
top3.whyItMatters: Leaderboard ranks can be wrong by double digits, so test agents on your own work.

items.title: Data centers lost at the ballot box in the US midterms
items.takeaway: Thompson: anti-data-center ads ran in Wisconsin; Texas governor-elect pledged a construction moratorium.
items.soWhat: Texas holds over a quarter of planned US capacity, so build-out timelines face real political risk.

items.title: ChatGPT keeps pointing users to a scam clone of T3 Code
items.takeaway: A user asked for the T3 Code download and got t33.codes; founder Theo says it happens constantly.
items.soWhat: AI answers can send staff to fake download sites, so verify domains before installing tools.

items.title: Claude Code loosens its rule against recreating existing games
items.takeaway: Naming a game to describe mechanics now yields an original game in that genre, per Addy Osmani.
items.soWhat: Vendors are tuning hidden prompt rules on the fly, which can change what your agents will build.

items.title: Tavi Costa sees opportunity as top copper miners' output falls 16%
items.takeaway: He says the largest miners face their lowest annual production in nearly 15 years; chart source not named.
items.soWhat: Power and data center build-outs need copper, so supply limits could raise infrastructure costs.

items.title: Altman says the need for human control should constrain AI progress
items.takeaway: OpenAI's CEO says people should not cede control of the future to superintelligence.
items.soWhat: Watch whether OpenAI's products and policy asks match this stated limit on its own progress.

items.title: Meng To calls Vercel's Geist the anti-slop font
items.takeaway: He points to vercel.com/font and Vercel's Oct 30 launch of Geist Serif.
items.soWhat: A distinct, well-made typeface is a cheap way to keep AI-built interfaces from looking generic.

items.title: Cloudflare embedded security engineers in US newsrooms on election night
items.takeaway: Matthew Prince says the Athenian Project helped critical news outlets report results without cyber disruption.
items.soWhat: High-stakes nights now get on-site security support, a model for any critical launch or event.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.318 warns before stored sign-ins expire
items.takeaway: Also lets side jobs run at low effort and fixes compaction and resumed-workflow bugs.
items.soWhat: Unattended agent jobs fail quietly when logins lapse, so this early warning saves broken runs.

items.title: Vercel ships a doctor command so agents can fix CLI setup
items.takeaway: vercel doctor lists fix commands, needs no login, never prompts, and outputs JSON.
items.soWhat: Tools built for agents to self-repair cut support load, so ask vendors for the same.

items.title: Researchers screen agent skills for malware by reading model hidden states
items.takeaway: LatentTriad reports 99% F1 across 5,830 skill packages without running any skill code.
items.soWhat: Skill marketplaces are an attack surface, and cheap pre-install scanning is becoming feasible.

image.alt: arXiv 2611.05088: Researchers screen agent skills for malware by reading model hidden states

items.title: Grading errors silently reorder popular AI agent leaderboards
items.takeaway: An audit of HAL and tau2-bench found ungraded episodes stored as failures; maintainers confirmed three errors.
items.soWhat: Don't pick an agent vendor on leaderboard rank alone; ask how results were graded.

image.alt: arXiv 2611.04399: Grading errors silently reorder popular AI agent leaderboards

items.title: Fake hazard warnings steer agents past injection filters
items.takeaway: A fabricated review steered agents 60% of the time; requiring corroboration cut exposure about 95%.
items.soWhat: Tell agents to corroborate warnings before acting, since detectors miss this attack.

image.alt: arXiv 2611.04393: Fake hazard warnings steer agents past injection filters

items.title: Claude Code lets failed safety hooks block agent actions
items.takeaway: 2.1.317 adds onFailure block for Agent SDK hooks and asks before tools send the account email out.
items.soWhat: Guardrails that fail open are not guardrails, so switch critical hooks to block.
